# Issue #468: POC step 2: decode the BDHb heap of pylavi add.vi into a tag tree and locate one editable logic field

## Goal
The goal requires a proof of concept (POC) before more benchmark work: an agent that never saw a VI describes its diagram and changes its logic without LabVIEW. Step 1 (#465, saved on this branch) measured that `pylavi/tests/add.vi` (sha256 cf4b1f56...) has a zlib BDHb payload of 842 bytes, readable without LabVIEW, but did not decode it; it ended partial on input_budget (864k input in 15 turns). Expected gain: a decoded heap tag tree and one concrete candidate byte change (primitive id or constant value), so the next session can order the edit step or report POC exits. Check: README line `heap-decode: yes|partial|no`.

## Work
1. Read docs/research/poc/README.md (on this branch). Do not repeat the step 1 container measurements.
2. Write stdlib `docs/research/poc/inspect_vi.py` (python3 -I, path as argument): parse RSRC, decompress BDHb (offset 4 inside payload), then parse the heap after its UInt32 length as a stream of entries. Hypothesis to test: each entry starts with a 16-bit header encoding entry scope (open/close/leaf), tag id and attribute count/size, as in the published LabVIEW heap format notes (pylabview `LVheap`). Report the parse as an indented tag tree; stop and record where the parse fails.
3. Run the same parser on 2-3 other small pylavi test VIs (for example empty_separate_code.vi) and compare: tags present only in add.vi are diagram-node candidates.
4. Update README.md: decoded tree summary (at most 60 lines), which tags are identified with evidence, explicit gaps, one candidate logic change with exact offsets inside the decompressed heap, and what must be re-encoded (zlib, Adler-32, BDHb length, RSRC offsets). End with `heap-decode: yes|partial|no` and evidence. Keep the `poc-feasibility:` line and update it.

## Acceptance
- [ ] inspect_vi.py runs with python3 -I on add.vi and prints a tag tree or a stated parse-failure offset.
- [ ] README.md has `heap-decode:` and `poc-feasibility:` lines with evidence; undecoded parts listed as gaps.
- [ ] No LabVIEW behaviour is claimed; opening in LabVIEW stays an owner check.

## Verification
`python3 -c "import sys; t=open('docs/research/poc/README.md').read(); sys.exit(not ('heap-decode:' in t and 'poc-feasibility:' in t))"`

## Context
- docs/research/poc/README.md: step 1 results and container offsets.
- benchmark/scripts/sources.py::save_version and $LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/pylavi/pylavi/file.py: RSRC parsing to reuse (read, do not edit benchmark/).
- Do not run git commit; the parent commits. Do not use git diff in checks.

## Budget
- Stay below 350k input tokens. Step 1 spent 864k: avoid large reads.
- Never print more than 128 bytes of hex or 80 lines of output per command; write long output to a file under docs/research/poc/ and read slices.
- Do not read docs/research/0002-delivery.md in full (grep it). Do not read whole benchmark JSON files.
- Write README.md early (after the first parser run) and update it.

# POC: inspect one public VI without LabVIEW

## Measured result so far

The RSRC container and compressed block diagram of `pylavi/tests/add.vi` are readable without LabVIEW. Diagram semantics and an executable logic edit remain unverified; this is an initial research checkpoint, not a successful editing demonstration.

## Selected artifact and provenance

- Original path: `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/pylavi/tests/add.vi` (prepared public source, read-only).
- Upstream: https://github.com/marcpage/pylavi/tree/35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75 ; license: Unlicense.
- File size: 6,371 bytes; SHA256: `cf4b1f56c8e42a7a353101ba1322aa3d64207bb19df5dc791cb3eedf2bb2f7e8`.
- RSRC format: 3, file type `LVIN`, creator `LBVW`.
- Saved-version bytes: `21008000`, representing LabVIEW 21.0.0 final build 0, in `LVSR` at absolute offset 36 and every observed `vers` entry (IDs 4, 7, 8, 9, 10; offsets 1532, 1548, 1564, 1580, 1596). These are original artifact declarations, not runtime compatibility evidence.

## Observations from original bytes

`BDHb` resource 0 has a 477-byte payload at absolute offset 4032. Its first four bytes are `0000034a` (842); zlib decompression beginning at payload offset 4 returns exactly 842 bytes. Decompression at offsets 0 and 8 fails. The decompressed prefix is `00000346101802fe007efd000210f502fe001bfd000364cb084000114e01fb0004`; the leading UInt32 is 838, equal to the remaining decompressed byte count. This exposes a compact binary heap, not textual node or primitive names.

The source inventory and container interpretation reuse the research in [0002-delivery.md](../0002-delivery.md), `benchmark/scripts/sources.py::save_version`, and pinned upstream `pylavi/pylavi/file.py`. None of those sources decodes block diagram semantics. `benchmark/native/readiness-case.json` supplies saved-property expectations for other public fixtures, not an arithmetic oracle for this file. The filename `add.vi` is a selection hint, not evidence that its diagram performs addition.

## Explicit gaps and candidate change

Nodes, primitive identities, constant values, terminal identities, wire endpoints and execution behavior have not yet been decoded. The candidate is to replace an arithmetic Add primitive with Subtract if a primitive discriminator and compatible terminals can be established from evidence. No responsible byte patch can yet be specified; locating that field is the next measurement.

## Container consistency and native risk

The original header declares data offset 32, data size 4980, metadata offset 5012 and metadata size 1359; its duplicated header starts at 5012. A changed compressed payload needs its resource length, four-byte alignment, subsequent resource offsets, both headers' data size and metadata offset, and any affected metadata-relative offsets kept consistent. Recompression must update the zlib stream and its Adler-32 checksum; a same-length decompressed edit preserves the outer uncompressed-size prefix and inner heap length. Unknown semantic signatures, compiled-code consistency and heap invariants remain gaps. `BDPW` contains 48 bytes; the pinned pylavi parser identifies the first 16 as a password MD5 but does not establish the meaning or update rules of the remaining bytes.

No LabVIEW was executed. Opening without a broken arrow, changed behavior and preservation of the save version after an edit remain owner checks. A byte-level decoder or successful decompression alone cannot establish them.

poc-feasibility: partial — container and diagram decompression measured; semantic decoding and a concrete patch are still under investigation.

# Environment readiness

The owner requires the entire loop to execute in the cloud. Their Windows machine
is not a runner. Public source preparation and model access checks run on GitHub
hosted Ubuntu. Official NI headless automation is now verified in the cloud;
interactive IDE access is not part of this setup path.
The product goal is unchanged and no artifact family has been excluded.

Version requirement clarified by the owner on 18 October 2026: prioritize all
LabVIEW versions; LabVIEW 2024 is the accepted fallback if investigation shows
substantially greater time is needed for all versions. Estimate that difference
before choosing a version scope. No numeric time threshold was agreed. The local
LabVIEW 2026 observation does not verify LabVIEW 2024 or cross-version compatibility.

## Reproducible public sources

`policy/prepare.sh` calls `.github/loop/prepare_environment.py` from the session's checkout. It needs Python 3.10+
and git, no secrets, pip installations or NI activation. Sources and exact commits
are in `.github/loop/environment-sources.json`:

- NI Actor Framework, MIT, commit `371c631c16155d88f02be11a953e4964d7452fd8`.
- pylavi, Unlicense, commit `35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75`.

The check fetches these commits, rejects tracked modifications in its cache,
checks license markers and the SHA256 of one real NI VI, loads its resource table
with the pinned parser, and parses a real LabVIEW project as XML. It writes
`readiness.json` and exposes the cache as `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` to subsequent job
steps. Default cache: `$RUNNER_TEMP/connectwithlabview-environment`.
Public copies stay outside git. No NI installation files or personal projects are
redistributed. Downloads require outbound HTTPS to GitHub.

Preparation passed twice in a clean Linux Python 3.12 container and on Windows
Python 3.14. The checked VI contains 30 resource types; this is evidence of resource
access, not correctness of diagram interpretation. The public project reports
LVVersion `20008000`. Broader coverage and independent expected answers belong to
the evaluator/benchmark work; do not use parser output as its own sole oracle.

Hosted confirmation: [Environment readiness, run 39073653443](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/actions/runs/39073653443)
on 18 October 2026 (Europe/Warsaw) passed public source preparation and its second
invocation on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04.

The engine test suite passed on Linux/Python 3.12: 263 tests, 11 skipped
(template-only and opt-in live checks). This includes the routing and probe
classification tests. It does not validate unfinished adapter integration.

## Cloud provider access checks

`.github/workflows/environment.yml` runs on setup-branch changes to environment
code, and can be dispatched after GitHub registers the workflow. It does not call
the loop, merge work, or enable `AUTOPILOT`. Repository Actions are enabled; the
provider jobs need `contents: read` plus their provider permissions. Setup proof
jobs additionally need `contents: write` for separate task refs, state and
checkpoint assets; they do not merge to the default branch. No custom
runner is registered. `AUTOPILOT=off` is explicit during setup.

Pinned CLI packages are recorded in `.github/loop/cloud-providers.json`. Each
provider job installs just its CLI, calls a fixed probe in an isolated temporary
home, and uploads a summary, never credentials or raw model streams. A missing
secret, exhausted quota or failed response fails that readiness check. Generic
429/network failures remain unknown; they do not prove a depleted subscription.

| Provider | Repository secret | Access semantics |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | The owner created a supported long-lived token with `claude setup-token` and replaced the secret on 18 October 2026. Hosted probes reach the service but report subscription exhaustion. Track eventual replacement in the credential lifecycle. |
| Codex | Maintenance environment `CODEX_CI_AUTH_JSON`; execution `CODEX_WORKER_AUTH_JSON` | The owner provisioned the dedicated CI login and scoped App. Sequential cloud runners verified forced renewal and write-back; workers receive only access tokens. |
| Copilot | Job `GITHUB_TOKEN`, passed as `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` | The readiness job now requests `copilot-requests: write` and checks the pinned CLI. Current GitHub documentation supports this in personally owned repositories against the owner's seat. The earlier copied OAuth token remains stored but is no longer passed by this readiness job. |

The owner requested access to these accounts for cloud execution. Bootstrap values
were transferred directly to encrypted repository secrets without printing them.
They are not a complete unattended credential-renewal system. No API billing mode,
automatic credit purchase or provider substitution has been enabled.

The [credential requirements and accepted public repository](cloud-authentication.md)
record verified renewal requirements and cloud evidence. The owner explicitly
retained this public repository on 18 October 2026 and rejected a private control
repository. OpenAI's account-auth CI deployment recommendation covers private
automation; that recommendation does not cover the chosen layout. Trusted workflow
and credential-isolation checks must replace that assumption. No visibility or
billing change has been made.

Local diagnostic observations before adopting the cloud-only constraint: Claude
2.1.292 was authenticated but its real call reported a weekly subscription limit,
reset 20 October 2026 at 21:00 Europe/Warsaw. Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 and Copilot
1.0.98 returned their expected probe answers. Those local observations do not by
themselves prove cloud access. The hosted workflow's summaries are the cloud evidence.

That hosted run returned `available` with an actual model answer for Codex and
Copilot, and `quota` for Claude. The overall run therefore correctly failed
readiness. Claude's cloud call reached the service and reported a subscription
limit; it did not produce a usable model answer. These observations are point-in-time
checks, not promises of availability or durable token renewal.

## Required multi-provider execution

The owner accepted [Cloud model selection and quota management](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/11).
The existing engine still launches Claude. Installing the other CLIs does not
integrate task execution, stream accounting, permissions or the watchdog.

`provider_pool.py` is a deterministic building block, with tests. Owner configuration
defines the allowed provider/model catalog and bounded retry delays; policy supplies
an ordered list of candidates for each task class. Selection distinguishes model
and provider limits, requires a probe after reset, never invents fallback models,
and waits when all candidates are limited. Authentication failures remain blocked
until explicitly updated. The caller must persist state and implement probes,
provider adapters and checkpoint continuation. No live model catalog is accepted
or inferred by this module.

The integration must replace specific Claude guarantees for both other providers:
secret isolation from tool subprocesses, offline command networking, write scopes,
ignored task-branch configuration/hooks, time/turn limits, usage accounting and
limit/reset parsing. Copilot output redaction alone is not credential isolation.
Do not arm the loop until these checks and the other setup topics are resolved.

## LabVIEW cloud runtime and version coverage

The local diagnostic found only one actual LabVIEW executable: 32-bit LabVIEW 2026
26.1.1f1, plus NI LabVIEW CLI. The CLI connected to LabVIEW and completed an operation
help request. A direct COM probe did not open an example successfully. These local
findings alone did not prove scripting or cloud operation; the hosted check below
now supplies separate cloud runtime evidence.
Directories named for older releases were not counted as installed editors.

The owner's expanded NI License Manager screenshot, supplied on 18 October 2026,
confirms LabVIEW 2026 Q1 Community Edition is Licensed until 27 June 2027.
Professional Development System is Unlicensed; Base, Full, Continuous Integration
and Debug Deployment show Evaluation Available, not active licenses. This screenshot
supersedes the earlier uncertainty from package metadata. It establishes local
Community activation, not activation of LabVIEW 2024 or a cloud machine. No
activation was changed and no private project, serial number or NI license file
was uploaded.

NI's Community usage guidance permits personal, non-commercial, non-industrial
projects and lists free open-source projects as an example. The owner explicitly
confirmed a private, non-commercial project on 18 October 2026. The public download page does not confirm authenticated
access to the 2024 installer. Native 2024 activation/execution remains unverified;
the selected official headless runtime does not require desktop activation for
its supported automation operations.

## Official NI cloud automation path

[NI's official container project](https://github.com/ni/labview-for-containers)
and [headless guide](https://github.com/ni/labview-for-containers/blob/2afb30b23bdb144368ee36d5f5ca33c06f800a98/docs/headless-labview.md)
provide a cloud automation path that does not need desktop activation for supported
non-development operations. The setup uses the owner's active Community development
license and confirmed personal use for a bounded analysis/build check. Applying
the development-license container terms to that combination is an interpretation
of the published terms, not a specific NI statement about this project. No paid-only
condition or explicit Community exclusion was found. See the
[NI agreement](https://www.ni.com/content/dam/web/pdfs/legal/software_license_agreement_en.pdf),
Addendum F, and [Community guidance](https://www.ni.com/en/support/documentation/supplemental/20/labview-community-edition-usage-details.html).

The container is for automation/analysis/testing; it must not be used to author or
edit LabVIEW source. No public LabVIEW service or redistributed container image is
created. The readiness workflow mounts only a disposable fixture directory, has
no model/account secrets, and disables container networking. It mass-compiles an
existing public MIT fixture and collects operation logs and package versions.
Compilation is an environment check, not product development or the benchmark.

Pins and input provenance live in `.github/loop/labview-runtime.json`; the public
workflow is `.github/workflows/labview-runtime.yml`. The image is NI's LabVIEW
2026 Q1 Linux release, pinned by digest. Its fixture comes from the pinned pylabview
LV2014 example and is SHA256-checked before use. Successful processing proves
that this runtime can load/compile that input; it does not prove semantic reading,
all-version compatibility, VI Scripting availability, or native LabVIEW 2024.

The official registry lists no LabVIEW 2024 image as of 18 October 2026. A separate
2024 installer/activation path remains to be investigated if native 2024 execution
is needed. Using the newer runtime for this setup check does not select the fallback
or change the owner's goal of all versions.

### Hosted result, 18 October 2026

[LabVIEW cloud runtime run 39113730426](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/actions/runs/39113730426)
passed on hosted Ubuntu 24.04. LabVIEWCLI connected to native LabVIEW, completed
MassCompile and CloseLabVIEW, and the job exited successfully. The installed core
package is `26.1.0.49387-0+f235`. The source SHA256 was
`b6f8934ee58eb3418902b181379064aa77e558cb33f46e45bb179a96b235dd8a`;
the disposable compiled copy became
`406813850fb2fd931248f4fb7c997d9d597f6486704d5ebb4f57074cb1124ac9`.
Only logs/package information and the JSON summary were uploaded, not VI files
or a container image. No NI login, model secrets or outgoing container network
was needed. The first attempt exposed an inherited-output pipe waiting after
compilation; replacing the pipe with file capture resolved it, as the successful
run verifies.

[Environment readiness run 39113286966](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/actions/runs/39113286966)
also passed 284 engine tests (11 skipped), public-source preparation, isolation,
Codex and Copilot model probes. Claude correctly remained `quota`; the workflow
did not call it available. The run included the guarded Codex credential-store
steps, but full lifecycle failure/recovery and multi-provider task execution still
belong to the separate integration topic.

NI's published [software license agreement](https://www.ni.com/content/dam/web/pdfs/legal/software_license_agreement_en.pdf)
and [Community usage guidance](https://www.ni.com/en/support/documentation/supplemental/20/labview-community-edition-usage-details.html)
were used to assess the confirmed Community license and personal use. The cloud
baseline uses GitHub-hosted Ubuntu and the official headless image for analysis/build
automation under the interpretation stated above. No license or cloud VM purchase
was made, and no account activation or licensed local installation was transferred.

The environment baseline records tested public sources, a native cloud runtime,
account-access observations and known restrictions. It does not accept a new
product success gate. Shared availability, ordinary task adapters, credential
lifecycle recovery and continuation across limits belong to the owner-approved
multi-provider integration topic; its later implementation and verification are
recorded in [cloud authentication](cloud-authentication.md). Native 2024 execution,
all-version compatibility and full semantic reading remain unverified and must
not be reported as solved by this environment check.

The access/preparation topic was resolved with these explicit boundaries in
[its resolution](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/2#issuecomment-6248028771).
The owner accepted the multi-provider integration on 18 October 2026 with the
successful Claude task deferred because of subscription exhaustion. See the
explicit exception in [cloud authentication](cloud-authentication.md). Arming
still belongs to the final setup topic; AUTOPILOT remains off.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Research-only RSRC/BDHb inspector; stdlib, no LabVIEW or third-party imports.

Run: python3 -I docs/research/poc/inspect_vi.py path/to/add.vi
Offsets named heap_* include the decompressed heap's leading UInt32.
Grammar: pinned pylabview LVheap.py / LVmisc.py; see source-provenance.json.
This reads structural tags, not executable LabVIEW behavior.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import struct
import sys
import zlib

MAX_HEAP = 64 * 1024 * 1024


class ParseError(ValueError):
    pass


def require(ok, message):
    if not ok:
        raise ParseError(message)


def rsrc_resources(raw):
    require(len(raw) >= 32, 'truncated RSRC header')
    sig, check, fmt, kind, creator, meta, meta_size, start, size = struct.unpack_from('>4s2sH4s4sIIII', raw)
    require(sig == b'RSRC' and check == b'\r\n' and fmt == 3, 'requires RSRC format 3')
    require(start == 32 and start + size == meta and meta + meta_size <= len(raw), 'invalid RSRC bounds')
    require(meta_size >= 56 and raw[meta:meta + 32] == raw[:32], 'invalid secondary header')
    base = meta + 52
    count = struct.unpack_from('>I', raw, base)[0] + 1
    require(count <= (meta_size - 56) // 12, 'invalid resource type count')
    resources = []
    for index in range(count):
        name, minus_one, offset = struct.unpack_from('>4sII', raw, base + 4 + index * 12)
        table, entries = base + offset, minus_one + 1
        require(table >= base + 4 + count * 12 and table + entries * 20 <= meta + meta_size, 'invalid resource table')
        for entry in range(entries):
            rid, _, _, relative, _ = struct.unpack_from('>IIIII', raw, table + entry * 20)
            location = start + relative
            require(start <= location and location + 4 <= meta, 'invalid resource offset')
            length = struct.unpack_from('>I', raw, location)[0]
            require(location + 4 + length <= meta, 'truncated resource payload')
            resources.append({'type': name.decode('ascii', 'replace'), 'id': rid,
                              'payload_offset': location + 4, 'payload_length': length})
    return resources


class Cursor:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data, self.pos = data, 4

    def take(self, n):
        require(0 <= n <= len(self.data) - self.pos, f'truncated field at heap offset {self.pos}; requested {n}')
        result = self.data[self.pos:self.pos + n]
        self.pos += n
        return result

    def integer(self, n, signed=False):
        return int.from_bytes(self.take(n), 'big', signed=signed)

    def u124(self):
        first = self.integer(1)
        return self.integer({255: 2, 254: 4}[first]) if first in (255, 254) else first

    def s124(self):
        first = self.integer(1, True)
        return self.integer({-128: 2, -127: 4}[first], True) if first in (-128, -127) else first

    def s24(self):
        first = self.integer(2, True)
        return self.integer(4, True) if first == -32768 else first


def parse_heap(heap):
    cursor, entries, stack = Cursor(heap), [], []
    entry_start = 0
    try:
        require(len(heap) >= 4, 'missing heap length')
        declared = int.from_bytes(heap[:4], 'big')
        require(declared == len(heap) - 4, f'heap length {declared} differs from {len(heap) - 4}')
        while cursor.pos < len(heap):
            entry_start = cursor.pos
            header = cursor.integer(2)
            size_spec, has_attrs, scope = header >> 13, bool(header & 0x1000), (header >> 10) & 3
            raw_tag = header & 1023
            tag = cursor.integer(4, True) if raw_tag == 1023 else raw_tag - 31
            require(scope in (0, 1, 2), f'reserved scope {scope}')
            require(size_spec != 5, 'unsupported sizeSpec 5')
            attrs = []
            if has_attrs:
                count = cursor.u124()
                require(count <= (len(heap) - cursor.pos) // 3, 'attribute count exceeds remaining bytes')
                for _ in range(count):
                    attr_start = cursor.pos
                    attr_id = cursor.s124()
                    value_offset = cursor.pos
                    value = cursor.s24()
                    attrs.append({'id': attr_id, 'value': value, 'heap_offset': attr_start,
                                  'value_offset': value_offset, 'end': cursor.pos})
            data_size = cursor.u124() if size_spec == 6 else size_spec if 1 <= size_spec <= 4 else 0
            data_offset = cursor.pos
            content = cursor.take(data_size)
            if scope == 2:
                require(bool(stack), 'close without open')
                require(stack[-1] == tag, f'close tag {tag} differs from open {stack[-1]}')
                stack.pop()
            entry = {'heap_offset': entry_start, 'end': cursor.pos, 'header': header,
                     'scope': ('open', 'leaf', 'close')[scope], 'tag': tag, 'depth': len(stack),
                     'size_spec': size_spec, 'attributes': attrs, 'data_offset': data_offset,
                     'data_length': data_size, 'content_hex': content.hex()}
            if size_spec in (0, 7):
                entry['inline_bool'] = size_spec == 7
            entries.append(entry)
            if scope == 0:
                stack.append(tag)
        require(not stack, f'{len(stack)} unclosed tags at end')
        return {'status': 'complete', 'consumed': cursor.pos, 'entries': entries}
    except ParseError as exc:
        return {'status': 'partial', 'failure_entry_offset': entry_start,

def inspect(path):
    raw = Path(path).read_bytes()
    resources = rsrc_resources(raw)
    matches = [r for r in resources if r['type'] == 'BDHb' and r['id'] == 0]
    require(len(matches) == 1, 'expected exactly one BDHb resource id 0')
    resource = matches[0]
    offset = resource['payload_offset']
    payload = raw[offset:offset + resource['payload_length']]
    require(len(payload) >= 6, 'truncated BDHb')
    declared = int.from_bytes(payload[:4], 'big')
    require(4 <= declared <= MAX_HEAP, 'invalid or unsupported BDHb uncompressed size')
    stream = zlib.decompressobj()
    heap = stream.decompress(payload[4:], declared + 1)
    require(stream.eof and not stream.unused_data and not stream.unconsumed_tail, 'incomplete or trailing zlib stream')
    require(len(heap) == declared, 'BDHb decompressed-size mismatch')
    parsed = parse_heap(heap)
    return {'artifact': str(path), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
            'heap_sha256': hashlib.sha256(heap).hexdigest(), 'resource': resource,
            'heap_bytes': len(heap), 'heap_length': int.from_bytes(heap[:4], 'big'), **parsed}


def load_labels():
    path = Path(__file__).with_name('heap-labels.json')
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}


def tree_lines(result, labels):
    tags = {**labels.get('SL_SYSTEM_TAGS', {}), **labels.get('OBJ_FIELD_TAGS', {})}
    classes = labels.get('SL_CLASS_TAGS', {})
    attrs = labels.get('SL_SYSTEM_ATTRIB_TAGS', {})
    lines = []
    for entry in result['entries']:
        tag = entry['tag']
        name = tags.get(str(tag), f'tag({tag})')
        marker = {'open': '+', 'leaf': '=', 'close': '-'}[entry['scope']]
        details = []
        for attr in entry['attributes']:
            value = classes.get(str(attr['value']), str(attr['value'])) if attr['id'] == -2 else str(attr['value'])
            details.append(f"{attrs.get(str(attr['id']), str(attr['id']))}={value}")
        content = bytes.fromhex(entry['content_hex'])
        if content:
            value = str(int.from_bytes(content, 'big')) if len(content) <= 4 else f'{len(content)} bytes'
            details.append(f"data@{entry['data_offset']}={value}")
        elif entry['scope'] == 'leaf':
            details.append(f"inline={entry.get('inline_bool')}")
        lines.append(f"{entry['heap_offset']:04d} {'  ' * entry['depth']}{marker} {name} [{tag}] {' '.join(details)}".rstrip())
    return lines


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('path')
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, help='save complete JSON evidence')
    parser.add_argument('--tree-output', type=Path, help='save full indented tree')
    parser.add_argument('--max-lines', type=int, default=60)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = inspect(args.path)
        lines = tree_lines(result, load_labels())
        if args.output:
            args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
        if args.tree_output:
            args.tree_output.write_text('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
        print(f"artifact={result['artifact']} sha256={result['sha256']}")
        print(f"heap_bytes={result['heap_bytes']} entries={len(lines)} parse={result['status']}; offsets include heap UInt32")
        print('\n'.join(lines[:max(0, min(args.max_lines, 70))]))
        if len(lines) > args.max_lines:
            print(f'{len(lines) - max(0, args.max_lines)} tree lines omitted; use --tree-output for all entries')
        if result['status'] != 'complete':
            print(f"PARSE FAILURE entry@{result['failure_entry_offset']} cursor@{result['failure_cursor_offset']}: {result['reason']}")
            return 1
        print(f"COMPLETE consumed={result['consumed']}; scopes balanced, inner/outer lengths and zlib checksum valid")
        return 0
    except (OSError, ValueError, struct.error, zlib.error) as exc:
        print(f'PARSE FAILURE: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

"""Offline structural checks against pinned primary-source field readers.

Run: python3 -I docs/research/poc/verify_poc.py
Writes verification.json and candidate-change.json beside this script.
No original or edited VI is written; the candidate mutation stays in memory.

import ast
from hashlib import sha256
import importlib.util
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import types
import warnings
import zlib

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
warnings.simplefilter('ignore', SyntaxWarning)
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('inspect_vi', HERE / 'inspect_vi.py')
inspector = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(inspector)


def source_function(path, name, namespace):
    module = ast.parse(path.read_text())
    functions = [n for n in ast.walk(module) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name]
    assert len(functions) == 1, name
    compiled = ast.Module(body=functions, type_ignores=[])
    exec(compile(compiled, str(path), 'exec'), namespace)
    return namespace[name]


def original_heap(path, result):
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    resource = result['resource']
    start = resource['payload_offset']
    return zlib.decompress(raw[start + 4:start + resource['payload_length']])


def main():
    provenance = json.loads((HERE / 'source-provenance.json').read_text())
    for record in provenance:
        assert sha256((HERE / record['file']).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == record['sha256']
    misc_ns = {}
    misc = types.SimpleNamespace(**{name: source_function(HERE / 'LVmisc-source.txt', name, misc_ns)
                                  for name in ('readVariableSizeFieldU124', 'readVariableSizeFieldS124', 'readVariableSizeFieldS24')})
    errors = []
    namespace = {'LVmisc': misc, 'attributeValueIntToIntOrEn': lambda key, val, obj: val,
                 'eprint': lambda *args: errors.append(str(args))}
    source_reader = source_function(HERE / 'LVheap-source.txt', 'parseRSRCData', namespace)
    evidence = {'scope': 'structural, no LabVIEW execution', 'primary_source_hashes': 'pass', 'fixtures': {}}
    root = Path(os.environ['LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT']) / 'pylavi/tests'
    labels = inspector.load_labels()

        # Correct length to reach the truncated last entry, rather than fail on the size prefix.

        evidence['fixtures'][name] = {'sha256': result['sha256'], 'entries': len(result['entries']),

# POC: inspect one public VI without LabVIEW

## Measured result

`add.vi` now has a completely framed BDHb tag tree: 162 entries consume all 842 decompressed bytes, with matching open/close tags. The tree identifies a primitive discriminator and three signal endpoint pairs. An in-memory discriminator mutation reparses successfully; its mathematical meaning and LabVIEW validity remain unverified. No VI was edited on disk and no LabVIEW behavior is claimed.

## Artifact and primary-source provenance

- Input: `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/pylavi/tests/add.vi`, pylavi [35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75](https://github.com/marcpage/pylavi/tree/35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75), Unlicense; SHA256 `cf4b1f56c8e42a7a353101ba1322aa3d64207bb19df5dc791cb3eedf2bb2f7e8`.
- Step 1 established the 6,371-byte RSRC format-3 `LVIN`/`LBVW` container and declared save version `21008000` (21.0.0 final build 0). Those measurements were reused, not repeated as a separate investigation. They establish artifact declarations, not runtime compatibility.
- Heap grammar and names come from pylabview [5f20e23de6a386021eb955c825cc43d221f09ff1](https://github.com/mefistotelis/pylabview/tree/5f20e23de6a386021eb955c825cc43d221f09ff1), `pylabview/LVheap.py` and `LVmisc.py`. [Source URLs and SHA256s](source-provenance.json), [MIT license](pylabview-LICENSE.txt), and exact [LVheap](LVheap-source.txt)/[LVmisc](LVmisc-source.txt) snapshots are saved. These are the upstream author's reverse-engineering rules, not an NI specification. The pinned wiki page contains no entry-level grammar; the executable source supplies it.
- RSRC traversal follows `benchmark/scripts/sources.py::save_version` and pinned pylavi `pylavi/file.py`; neither benchmark code nor prepared public artifacts were changed.

## Reproduce and inspect

```text
python3 -I docs/research/poc/inspect_vi.py /path/to/pylavi/tests/add.vi
python3 -I docs/research/poc/verify_poc.py
```

The inspector uses only stdlib and accepts a VI path; `heap-labels.json` supplies source-derived names beside the script. Without that sidecar it still prints numeric tags. `--output FILE` saves complete JSON offsets/content and `--tree-output FILE` saves the full tree; stdout defaults to 60 entries. Invalid input stops with the failing entry/cursor offset for heap errors, or a container/decompression diagnostic before heap parsing.

The 16-bit header hypothesis is confirmed structurally on all four fixtures: bits 15–13 are sizeSpec, bit 12 signals an attribute list, bits 11–10 encode open=0/leaf=1/close=2, and bits 9–0 contain tag+31. Raw tag 1023 introduces a signed UInt32-width tag ID. Attributes have a variable-width count and signed ID/value pairs. sizeSpec 1–4 gives literal body bytes; 6 introduces a variable-width body length; 0/7 encode no body/inline false/true. Reserved scope 3 and sizeSpec 5 stop this inspector. Sources: `LVheap.HeapNode.parseRSRCData`, `updateData`, `NODE_SCOPE`; `LVmisc.readVariableSizeField{U124,S124,S24}`.

Names depend on the nearest parent class (`LVheap.tagIdToEnum` and `CLASS_EN_TO_TAG_LIST_MAPPING`). In particular, text-hair tag 1 is `OF__flags`, not the global `OF__activeDiag`. All final JSON/tree files use this context. [First-run log](first-run.txt) preserves the initial framing checkpoint and is superseded for contextual names. Printed short bodies are unsigned raw integers; compound data remains uninterpreted bytes.
